questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
1. Report of the Group of Ministers on reforming the national security system
2. Creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff
3. Report of the Kargil Review Committee
4. Naresh Chandra Task Force on national security
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Kargil Review Committee under K. Subrahmanyam reported in 1999 on the lapses that led to the conflict. A Group of Ministers examined it and in 2001 recommended a Chief of Defence Staff. The Naresh Chandra Task Force of 2012 suggested a permanent chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee as a halfway step. The post was finally created in 2019, along with the Department of Military Affairs.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 60; the 2012 task force is static

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a fifth-generation fighter aircraft?
questions.e: The F-22 and F-35 of the United States, the Su-57 of Russia and the J-20 of China are the fifth-generation fighters in service, defined by stealth shaping, internal weapon bays, supercruise and fused sensors. The French Rafale, which India operates, is a 4.5-generation aircraft: highly capable but not designed around low observability. India's own programme aims at a prototype by the end of this decade and induction in the mid-2030s.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 61-62; Rafale's generation is static

questions.q:
The Indian Navy released its Maritime Security Strategy in 2026. With reference to India's naval strategy documents, consider the following pairs:
Document : Feature
1. Freedom to Use the Seas (2007) : Strategy shaped mainly by the 26/11 attacks, with the mandate widened to coastal and offshore security
2. Ensuring Secure Seas (2015) : Described India as a 'net security provider' in its maritime neighbourhood
3. Maritime Security Strategy, 2026 : First of the three to bring coastal and offshore security into the Navy's mandate
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 2 is correct. The 2007 document argued for an ocean-going navy, with sea control, forward presence and deterrence, in a defence outlook dominated by land borders; it came well before 26/11, so pair 1 is wrong. The 2015 document, written after the 26/11 attacks and with China's growing presence in mind, added coastal and offshore security and used the net security provider phrase. That makes pair 3 wrong too: the 2026 strategy is new in responding to grey-zone competition, new domains and disruptive technology.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (System in news in 2026)
A. Vayu Astra-1
B. NASM-SR
C. TARA
D. Mahendragiri
List-II (Description)
1. Stealth frigate of Project 17A
2. Glide weapon that turns unguided warheads into precision-guided ones
3. Loitering munition
4. Anti-ship missile with an imaging infra-red seeker
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Vayu Astra-1 is an indigenous loitering munition that completed high-altitude trials; such a drone circles, watches and then dives on the target. The short-range naval anti-ship missile of DRDO uses inertial navigation mid-course and an infra-red seeker at the end. TARA, tested with the Air Force, is India's first indigenous glide kit. Mahendragiri is a Nilgiri-class frigate delivered by Mazagon Dock.

questions.q: 'Captagon', a drug whose international trafficking syndicate was busted in India under Operation RAGEPILL, is
o: a concentrated resin obtained from cannabis
a hallucinogen extracted from certain mushrooms
a semi-synthetic opioid derived from the opium poppy
a synthetic amphetamine-type stimulant containing fenetylline
questions.e: Captagon tablets contain fenetylline, once prescribed for attention disorders and narcolepsy, along with amphetamine. It is a stimulant that suppresses fatigue and fear, and its use by militant groups in West Asia gave it the label 'jihadi drug'. It was banned internationally in the 1980s and is controlled under the UN psychotropic substances convention; in India it falls under the 1985 narcotics law. The Narcotics Control Bureau ran the operation.

questions.q:
A new Chief of Defence Staff was appointed in 2026. With reference to the post, consider the following statements:
1. The Chief of Defence Staff is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.
2. The Chief of Defence Staff is the military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority.
3. As Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs, the Chief of Defence Staff handles capital acquisitions for the three Services.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The holder is first among equals in the committee of Service Chiefs, and the notes list the role of military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority among the strategic mandates, along with theatre commands and policy planning. Statement 3 is wrong: the Department of Military Affairs deals with the armed forces and with procurement other than capital acquisitions, which stay with the Department of Defence. The post carries no military command over the Chiefs; it works through jointness and advice.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 60; Department of Military Affairs' remit is as stated in the notes

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Instrument or body : Description
1. UN Vienna Convention, 1988 : Deals with drug trafficking and laundering of its proceeds
2. Palermo Convention, 2000 : UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime
3. Financial Action Task Force : Inter-governmental standard-setting body of which India is a member
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three are correct. The 1988 convention on narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances required States to criminalise the laundering of drug money and to control precursor chemicals. The Palermo Convention widened this to organised crime generally, including laundering, corruption and obstruction of justice. The task force is not a treaty body; it issues recommendations and reviews members, India being one. India's own law on the subject dates from 2002.

questions.q: The TARA weapon tested in 2026 is described as a 'stand-off' weapon. This means that it
o: is fired from the ground to intercept incoming aircraft
can be launched only from a stationary platform
stays over the target area until a target appears
can be released from outside the reach of the enemy's air defences
questions.e: A stand-off weapon lets the aircraft stay beyond the range of hostile air-defence missiles. The glide kit gives an ordinary warhead wings and guidance, so that it travels more than eighty kilometres at high subsonic speed after release and strikes precisely. Staying over the target describes a loitering munition, and ground-launched interception describes a surface-to-air missile. Gaurav and the Smart Anti-Airfield Weapon are earlier Indian glide bombs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz are described as 'digital chokepoints'.
Statement-II: Many undersea fibre-optic cables converge in these narrow corridors.
Statement-III: Satellites carry the larger share of intercontinental data traffic, with cables serving as a back-up.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-II is correct and explains the first. Cables follow the shortest sea routes between Europe, West Asia and Asia, so many of them pass through the same narrow waters, where an accident or a hostile act can cut several at once. Statement-III is wrong: cables carry well over 95 per cent of international data and offer far more bandwidth at lower cost than satellites. Iran's proposal to charge cable operators highlighted this.

questions.q: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, from where the Divyastra missile was flight-tested in 2026, is located
o: in the Gulf of Mannar near Rameswaram
in the Andaman group north of Port Blair
off the coast of Odisha in the Bay of Bengal
off the coast of Andhra Pradesh near Sriharikota
questions.e: The island, earlier called Wheeler Island, lies off the Odisha coast and with Chandipur forms the Integrated Test Range used for most of India's missile trials. Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh is the space launch centre of ISRO, not a missile range. Rameswaram is associated with Dr Kalam's birthplace, which makes it a tempting but wrong choice, and the Andaman islands host a tri-service command.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 62; location is static

questions.q:
India conducted a second flight trial of the Divyastra missile in 2026. In this context, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A missile with MIRV technology makes it harder for an adversary's missile defence to intercept the attack.
Statement-II: In a MIRV system, all the warheads of a missile fall together on the same target.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not. In a MIRV system a single missile carries several warheads and each is steered to a different target, so the defender must deal with many incoming objects on separate paths. Warheads released together on one target describe the older multiple re-entry vehicle idea. Divyastra is an Agni missile with this capability; the United States developed it first, and Russia, Britain, France and China also have it.

questions.q: The 'No War No Peace' paradigm, which the Indian Navy's 2026 strategy takes as a starting point, refers to
o: a policy of keeping warships away from disputed waters in peacetime
continuous competition through grey-zone actions that stay below the threshold of open war
a doctrine of not being the first to use force at sea
a period of ceasefire supervised by a neutral naval force
questions.e: The strategy sets aside the older binary of war and peace. Rivals now use proxies, maritime militias, cyber-attacks, dual-use vessels and deniable operations to gain advantage without triggering a war. One of its five objectives is therefore to prevail below the threshold of conflict, through constant intelligence and calibrated, scalable responses, including autonomous systems, without unintended escalation. It is not a no-first-use or disengagement policy.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Stage of money laundering)
A. Placement
B. Layering
C. Integration
List-II (Typical method)
1. Taking a loan against one's own illicit deposit, so that the money returns as legitimate borrowing
2. Splitting cash into many small deposits made through money mules
3. Over-invoicing and under-invoicing of trade between shell companies
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Placement puts dirty cash into the financial system, typically by smurfing, casinos or cash-heavy front businesses. Layering hides the trail through complex transactions, such as mis-invoiced trade, shell companies in several countries, or conversion into property, gold and crypto-assets. Integration brings the money back looking clean, for example through back-to-back loans or resale of costly assets. The UN's 1988 Vienna Convention first defined laundering in this sense.

questions.q:
With reference to 'Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2025', consider the following statements:
1. It is brought out by an institute based in Stockholm.
2. Germany figures among the five largest military spenders.
3. India is ranked third among military spenders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, founded in 1966, publishes the data. The top five are the United States, China, Russia, Germany and India, together accounting for well over half of world spending; Germany's rearmament since the Ukraine war has put it ahead of India. Statement 3 is wrong, since India is fifth, though its spending rose over the previous year.

questions.q:
With reference to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft, whose programme facility was begun in Andhra Pradesh in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. 'Supercruise', a feature sought in it, means sustained supersonic flight with the afterburners kept on throughout.
2. It is being designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency.
3. Its first version is to use GE-F414 engines.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The agency under DRDO leads the design of this stealth, medium-weight multirole fighter; the first mark uses an American engine and a later mark is planned with an indigenous one. Statement 1 is wrong: supercruise is supersonic flight without afterburners, which burn a great deal of fuel and enlarge the heat signature. Stealth and integrated avionics are the other defining features of a fifth-generation aircraft.

questions.q: In maritime security, 'dark vessels' are ships that
o: sail only at night to save fuel in tropical waters
carry no national flag and so belong to no State
switch off their Automatic Identification System to avoid being tracked
are painted to reduce their visibility to radar and satellites
questions.e: Merchant ships must broadcast identity and position through a transponder. Vessels engaged in sanctions evasion, smuggling or illegal fishing turn it off, or spoof it, and are called dark vessels; groups of them carrying sanctioned oil are known as shadow fleets. The 2026 naval strategy lists them among maritime crimes, along with piracy, trafficking and illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. Tracking them needs satellites and information-fusion centres.

questions.q: The Home Ministry proposed a Smart Border Project in 2026. Which one of the following gives the correct descending order of India's neighbours by length of land border shared with India?
questions.e: Bangladesh has the longest border with India, about 4,097 km, followed by China at 3,488 km and Pakistan at 3,323 km. Nepal, at 1,751 km, is slightly ahead of Myanmar at 1,643 km; Bhutan and Afghanistan come last. The project covers the Bangladesh and Pakistan borders, using drones, radars and cameras where rivers, marshes and deserts make fencing and manual patrolling difficult.

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Navy's Maritime Security Strategy, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The National Maritime Security Coordinator, noted in it as part of higher defence reform, functions under the National Security Council Secretariat.
2. Coastal security is to rest on layered patrols by the Navy, the Coast Guard and the Marine Police, coordinated through Joint Operations Centres.
3. Deterrence is to rest on a survivable submarine-based nuclear deterrent together with a balanced conventional force.
4. It rules out the use of autonomous systems in responses below the threshold of conflict.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The coordinator's post gives a whole-of-government view of maritime governance. Coastal security uses three layers and treats fishing communities as eyes and ears. Deterrence combines ballistic-missile submarines with conventional strength, forward deployment and signalling. Statement 4 is wrong: the strategy expressly includes autonomous systems among the scalable, calibrated responses for contests short of war.

questions.q:
The National Investigation Agency flagged the use of TATP in a blast case. With reference to this explosive, consider the following statements:
1. It is rich in nitrogen, which makes it easy to pick up with conventional explosive detectors.
2. It is highly sensitive to heat, friction and impact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong. Triacetone triperoxide is an organic peroxide made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only; because it has no nitrogen, detectors designed for conventional nitrogen-based explosives can miss it. Statement 2 is correct. It is unstable and can go off from a knock, static or warmth, which earned it the name 'Mother of Satan'. Being fairly easy to make, it was used in the Paris, Brussels and Manchester attacks.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 63-64; absence of nitrogen is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of Indian research stations, listed in the Navy's 2026 strategy among India's maritime interests:
Station : Region
1. Maitri : Antarctica
2. Bharati : Arctic
3. Himadri : Antarctica
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. Maitri and Bharati are India's two working stations in Antarctica, the first in the Schirmacher Oasis and the second in the Larsemann Hills. Himadri is India's Arctic station, at Ny-Alesund in Svalbard, Norway. The stations appear in a naval strategy because polar research, sea routes and resources are part of India's wider maritime interests.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's 2026 naval strategy counts the Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor, the International North-South Transport Corridor and the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor among strategic corridors.
Statement-II: Such corridors lower India's dependence on vulnerable maritime chokepoints.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. About 95 per cent of India's trade by volume and most of its crude oil imports move by sea, much of it through a few narrow passages such as Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb and Malacca. Alternative routes to Russia's Far East, to Central Asia through Iran, and to Europe through West Asia spread that risk, which is why a naval document lists them.

questions.q:
With reference to agencies dealing with money laundering in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Directorate of Enforcement functions under the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance.
2. Besides the money-laundering law, the Directorate enforces the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 and the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.
3. The Financial Intelligence Unit-India is a wing of the Directorate of Enforcement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Directorate began in 1956 as an enforcement unit in the Department of Economic Affairs for the exchange-control law, but it now sits in the Department of Revenue. It handles the foreign exchange, money-laundering and fugitive offenders laws, which makes statement 2 right. Statement 3 is wrong. The Financial Intelligence Unit is a separate body that receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports and passes intelligence to enforcement agencies.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 58-60; FIU-IND's separate status is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about military exercises in the news in 2026:
1. CINBAX is a naval exercise between India and Vietnam.
2. PRAGATI 2026 was a multilateral naval exercise hosted by the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. CINBAX is a bilateral army exercise between India and Cambodia. PRAGATI 2026 was a multilateral exercise led by the Indian Army at Umroi in Meghalaya, with twelve partner armies from South and South-East Asia and the Indian Ocean; the name stands for Partnership of Regional Armies for Growth and Transformation in the Indian Ocean Region. Both show army-level outreach to partner countries in India's wider neighbourhood.

questions.q:
With reference to the Project 17A frigates, one of which was delivered to the Navy in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. All ships of the class are built at Mazagon Dock in Mumbai.
2. They are named after hill ranges of India.
3. They use a propulsion arrangement combining diesel engines and gas turbines.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Nilgiri, Udaygiri, Himgiri, Taragiri, Dunagiri and Mahendragiri are all hill names, and the ships use combined diesel or gas propulsion, cruising on diesels and sprinting on turbines. Statement 1 is wrong: the class is shared between Mazagon Dock and Garden Reach in Kolkata, Mahendragiri being the fourth from the Mumbai yard. The ships are follow-ons of the Shivalik class with better weapons and sensors.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 62-63; naming and second shipyard are static

questions.q:
With reference to action against money laundering in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Directorate of Enforcement's annual report for 2025-26 puts the conviction rate in decided money-laundering cases below ten per cent.
2. Guidelines issued in January 2026 brought service providers dealing in virtual digital assets under anti-money-laundering obligations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct: the financial intelligence unit's guidelines impose due-diligence and reporting duties on crypto-asset service providers, since such assets are used in the layering stage. Statement 1 is wrong. The report claims a conviction rate of about 94 per cent in cases that have been decided; the real criticism is different, namely that trials are slow and few cases reach a verdict, leaving a gap between assets attached and assets confiscated.
